findings.trigger: Load an opportunity page at offset 25, click the collection Previous button to offset 0, and delay or fail the page-zero request.
findings.evidence: The Previous handler at line 618 invalidates the old request and changes offset but does not clear items or opportunityPage. The fetch effect clears those only under offset > 0 at lines 242-246, so its offset-zero path leaves page-25 rows and headers intact while the new request is pending. The UI renders cards from those retained items and labels the page from offset, now page 1. On an ordinary page-zero request failure, the generic catch only sets error and finally clears loading; it never clears stale rows or metadata, making the mismatch persistent. A user can open a later-page row during the pending interval; open() writes the current offset zero into its detail URL/history. Existing browser cases test the opposite later-page bootstrap and active-tier reset, not this Previous-to-zero delayed/error path.
findings.impact: The public browse can display page-two records as page one, retain incorrect page metadata after a failed request, and open a need with the wrong return offset. This violates the bounded page and preserved Back-state contract despite green existing gates.
findings.required_correction: Treat both directions of page navigation as an explicit page-state transition. Clear or otherwise isolate outgoing rows and authoritative page metadata before an offset-zero replacement request, and ensure failed requests leave a truthful empty/error state rather than stale cards. Preserve token bootstrap/409 semantics and add delayed and failed Previous-to-zero browser cases, including inability to open stale rows and correct Back offset.
